newsitem.title: MEXICO: James Capel ups Mexico '97 GDP forecast to 5.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: James Capel ups Mexico '97 GDP forecast to 5.8 pct.

text.p: HSBC James Capel raised its forecast for Mexico's 1997 gross domestic product growth to 5.8 percent from 4.4 percent following stronger-than-expected second quarter growth of 8.8 percent.

Economist Gray Newman said in a report the second quarter growth was due to a strong rebound in manufacturing output coupled with the first significant improvement in consumer spending since the peso's collapse in 1994.
Although there are questions as to the accuracy of GDP methodology in measuring a consumer rebound in Mexico, Newman said the figures left little doubt that consumer spending has started to recover.

In an interview with Reuters, Newman said that in addition to revising up his year-end estimate for statistical reasons following the second quarter results, he also saw evidence the fast-paced growth would continue in the third quarter.
"The first glimpses of the third quarter look good," he said, adding that the year-end estimate of 5.8 percent was still conservative.
